prompt: Write a constraints document to support the design brief. (with_skill condition: use design-constraints skill with its inline rubric forcing function; without_skill condition: no skill reference.)

assertions.text: Strategic-vs-execution test passes — every constraint passes the operational test; no rendering-layer guidance (sizing, contrast, motion, copy patterns) appears as if it filters the exploration space
Applicable regulatory frameworks named — the author has identified the specific frameworks that constitute deal-breakers for this brief's audience and use case
Target surface(s) declared — first sentence states the target surface(s): specific surface, surface mix, or explicit `open` marker
Audience reach realities named where they filter viability — phrased as exploration-space filters; not as execution-layer accessibility-rendering rules
Cognitive / institutional / operational realities at the strategic level — phrased as filters on the exploration space, not as rendering rules for the prototype
Hard data and access realities surfaced where applicable — when the data, institutional relationship, or audience-side context doesn't exist
No execution-layer guidance — none of the cross-reference categories (typography, color, motion, contrast, sizing, copy patterns, response-time targets) appears in the body
No success criteria — design properties for evaluation and their failure-modes-of-overpursuit are absent (those belong in design-evaluation)
No research findings beyond what's needed to make a constraint relevant — research findings appear only where they ground a constraint's relevance
Empirical claims sourced or marked (Inferred) — sourced claims have citations; extensions are marked (Inferred); qualitative magnitude language used where no source is available
